about: SKILLREC1 (2026-11-04): skill recommendations by road advancement, Map 0 -> 24, side maps under their parent. A proposal only; no game file changed. Same rows as docs/skill-recommendations-2026-11-04.md. budget: tools/skill_costs.js budget() at printed stats (S, cap 1 = (3A + H) x m + S, N; Nnew = N with the proposed skills, the plain-card bonus lost); extraS = ENG22 theoretical prices for skills this branch does not have; refit = over: re-fit / fits as printed / frees room / unpriced (new skill) / no change. Decision SKILLREC1-1.

rows.reason: CONTENT9-1: swings before units without Quick, so "play it in front of their 2/5" is the lesson; Map 0's fights already show Quick.
rows.repeats: Hedgerow Shrew (Map 1), Feral Tomcat (Map 3) and Caiman Hatchling (5-A) are 2/4 Quick: the re-fit must keep it a 2/5-2/6 body, not a fourth 2/4.
rows.note: Alternative if the re-fit lands on 2/4: Pounce 1 (shown on Map 0, from the tutorial side map).

rows.reason: CONTENT9-1: dogs guard an ally (lore bible). Since ENG22 Guardian also takes the arrows and shots aimed at a neighbour, so it is a real job on the first maps.
rows.repeats: Badger Lumberjack (Map 1) is the next Guardian; Alpine Marmot (11) and Thorny Devil (18) move to Taunt below so Guardian is not everywhere.

rows.reason: The only glass attacker on Map 0: the shape is the lesson (trade it or protect it). DESIGN1-2: vanilla has value.
rows.repeats: Otter Paddler (0-T) and Meadow Rabbit (1) share the shape; they get Level 1 abilities instead.

rows.cardName: Crossed-Eyes / Cottontail / Duck Paddler / Chipmunk Forager / Earthworm
rows.reason: The baselines every other card is read against (CONTENT9-1). A starter that gets an ability gets it at Level 1 (DESIGN1-2, ENG22-4).
A minnow is a shoal. It splits the 2/4 starter pair; the Level 0 copy stays vanilla (the owner's Level 1 rule), so the tutorial is unchanged.
rows.repeats: Ant Scout and Bee Forager carry Swarm on Map 0 already.
rows.note: levelSkills "1". Not Tide: Pond Trout takes Tide (0-T), and two 2/4-2/5 Tide fish would be a new pair.

rows.reason: DESIGN1-6 / ENG22: one keyword for the Lumber-when-Ready family. Same rule and price.
A trout swims; plain Tide does not count toward the two skills. Splits the 2/5 starter pair.
rows.repeats: Guppy and Shallows Fry got Tide at Level 1 in ENG22.

rows.now: starter 3/3, no skill (same as House Cat 3/3)
rows.reason: Otters are the river people; Tide gives the otter starter the Pebble Beach link without a second skill.

rows.reason: A rabbit bolts into its burrow: the wall that hides when hurt, next to the plain wall Duck Paddler.
rows.repeats: Box Turtle (Map 4) is the other Cower.

rows.reason: The owner's pick (DESIGN1-2): its attack lifts the neighbours' next attack, so where it stands matters.
rows.repeats: Conch Herald (Map 2) is Inspiring 1 too: the Drummer now teaches it one map earlier.
rows.note: ENG22: budget reads over (16.3 / 13.16) until the owner re-fits it.

rows.reason: CONTENT9-1: dormice wake at night; Thistlewood has day and night, so "play it now or hold it for dusk" is the decision.
rows.repeats: Owl Sentinel (Map 1) and Trash Panda Trickster (2-B) are the other early night cards.

rows.reason: CONTENT9-1: road-folk economy, a blocker you are happy to lose, so trading it is a plan. Not Delivery: dying, not Ready, is the trigger.
rows.repeats: Gull Thief (On Kill: Lumber, Map 2) is the mirror image.

rows.reason: CONTENT9-1: a hedgehog; melee attackers take 1. Previews Map 2's Thorns.
rows.repeats: Pincushion Urchin (Map 2) Thorns 2, Quill-thorn Boar (12) Thorns 3: the Thorns line grows 1-2-3.

rows.now: 1/6 Swarm (same as Ant Scout 1/5 Swarm, Map 0)
rows.reason: The owner's new skill and carrier (11-04): after it hits, Haste and Evade for its next turn. A hit-and-run vole instead of a second ant.
rows.repeats: Snowshoe Hare (16) and Cinder Gecko (19-A) are the proposed second and third Skitter.
rows.note: Skitter unpriced: the budget column leaves it out.

rows.reason: The owner's day / night split of Crepuscular: a lookout that hits by day and holds by night. The first card to show the two values.
rows.repeats: Owl Sentinel (night) and Robin Redbreast (day) on the same list.
rows.note: Price with the split: uptime x (3A + H) per phase (project-state 7).

rows.reason: Two of Map 1's cards carry True Sight and nothing on Maps 0-5 is Invisible; the Woodcock Lookout keeps it. Frees a little budget room.
rows.repeats: Raven Scout (Map 6) takes True Sight where Booming Bittern's Invisible first appears.

rows.note: Evasive x1.18 on the stats: a large re-fit (about 1/14).

rows.repeats: Coral Reef Shark (Map 10) is the second Swimmer.

rows.reason: The 10-16 placement said "Moonpull waits past Map 10-20, as you asked"; it is back on Map 2. Poison 1 alone keeps the jelly's sting.
rows.repeats: Moonpull is on this card only.
rows.note: If the owner placed it on purpose, keep it.
